11412-the-mirror-of-literature-amusement.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. te on the south-west of Westminster Abbey, where was formerly the eleemosynary, or almonry, where the alms of the abbots were distributed. Howell in his _Londinopolis_, describes this as "the spot where the abbot of Westminster permitted Caxton to set up his press in the _Almonry_, or Ambry," the former of which names is still retained.

arxiv-2105-10864.title: Drag of Two Cylindrical Intruders in a Two-Dimensional Granular Environment
arxiv-2105-10864.creator: Takumi Kubota 1, Haruto Ishikawa 1, and Satoshi Takada 1,2
arxiv-2105-10864.description: Abstract The drag of two cylindrical intruders in a two-dimensional granular environment is numerically studied by the discrete element method. We find the yield force, below which the intruders cannot move because of interactions with the surrounding particles. Above the yield force, on the other hand, the intruders can move at a constant speed.

arxiv-2109-04762.title: Dual-State Capsule Networks for Text Classification
arxiv-2109-04762.creator: Piyumal Demotte, Surangika Ranathunga
arxiv-2109-04762.description: Abstract Text classification systems based on contextual embeddings are not viable options for many of the low resource languages. On the other hand, recently introduced capsule networks have shown performance in par with these text classification models. Thus, they could be considered as a viable alternative for text classification for languages that do not have pre-trained contextual embedding models.

arxiv-2112-06481.title: Giant enhancement of atom-molecule interaction with dynamic magnetic fields
arxiv-2112-06481.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by . 1
abstract

We demonstrated that the inelastic collisions of ultracold atom and heteronuclear molecule can be manipulated and decreased or accelerated by several orders of magnitude in laboratory practicable dynamic magnetic fields. The mechanism of dynamic magnetic field control is based on matching the spectral peak of the modulation function of pulsed magnetic field with the Floquet engineered resonance structure of the collision.

arxiv-2205-04596.title: When does dough become a bagel? Analyzing the remaining mistakes on ImageNet
arxiv-2205-04596.creator: Vijay Vasudevan, Benjamin Caine, Raphael Gontijo-Lopes, Sara Fridovich-Keil, Rebecca Roelofs {vrv, rofls}@google.com, Google Research, Brain Team, University of California, Berkeley
arxiv-2205-04596.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vijay Vasudevan, Benjamin Caine, Raphael Gontijo-Lopes, Sara Fridovich-Keil, Rebecca Roelofs {vrv, rofls}@google.com, Google Research, Brain Team, University of California, Berkeley. Image classification accuracy on the ImageNet dataset has been a barometer for progress in computer vision over the last decade. Several recent papers have questioned the degree to which the benchmark remains useful to the community [ 33 , 4 , 31 , 43 , 37 ] , yet innovations continue to contribute gains to performance, with today’s largest models achieving 90%+ top-1 accuracy.

arxiv-2208-13607.title: Explicit holography for vector models at finite N N , volume and temperature
arxiv-2208-13607.description: Abstract In previous work we constructed an explicit mapping between large N N vector models (free or critical) in d d dimensions and a non-local high-spin gravity theory on A ​ d ​ S d + 1 AdS_{d+1} , such that the gravitational theory reproduces the field theory correlation functions order by order in 1 / N 1/N .

arxiv-2305-10484.title: Introducing the monoclinic polymorph of the Kitaev magnet Na 2 Co 2 TeO 6
arxiv-2305-10484.creator: Emilie Dufault ∗, Faranak Bahrami ∗, Alenna Streeter, Xiaohan Yao, Enrique Gonzalez, Qiang Zhang, Fazel Tafti
arxiv-2305-10484.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Emilie Dufault ∗, Faranak Bahrami ∗, Alenna Streeter, Xiaohan Yao, Enrique Gonzalez, Qiang Zhang, Fazel Tafti. Recent theoretical studies have suggested that the low-energy Hamiltonian of honeycomb cobaltate systems could be dominated by anisotropic Kitaev interactions. Motivated by the theory, a honeycomb layered material Na 2 Co 2 TeO 6 with a hexagonal unit cell has been studied and found to exhibit antiferromagnetic (AFM) ordering at 27 K with two spin reorientation transitions at 15 and 5 K.

arxiv-2403-11095.title: PyroTrack: Belief-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning Path Planning for Aerial Wildfire Monitoring in Partially Observable Environments
arxiv-2403-11095.creator: Sahand Khoshdel, Qi Luo, Fatemeh Afghah
arxiv-2403-11095.description: Abstract Motivated by agility, 3D mobility, and low-risk operation compared to human-operated management systems of autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), this work studies UAV-based active wildfire monitoring where a UAV detects fire incidents in remote areas and tracks the fire frontline.

arxiv-2404-11801.title: Semiclassical bremsstrahlung from a charge radially falling into a Schwarzschild black hole
arxiv-2404-11801.creator: João P. B. Brito, Rafael P. Bernar, Atsushi Higuchi, Luís C. B. Crispino
arxiv-2404-11801.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by João P. B. Brito, Rafael P. Bernar, Atsushi Higuchi, Luís C. B. Crispino. A semiclassical investigation of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by a charged particle in a radially freely falling motion in Schwarzschild spacetime is carried out. We use quantum field theory at tree level to obtain the one-particle-emission amplitudes. We analyze and compare the energy spectrum and total energy released, which are calculated from these amplitudes, for particles with varying initial positions and for particles originating from infinity with varying kinetic energy.

arxiv-2502-11514.title: Investigating Inference-time Scaling for Chain of Multi-modal Thought: A Preliminary Study
arxiv-2502-11514.creator: Yujie Lin, Ante Wang, Moye Chen, Jingyao Liu, Hao Liu, Jinsong Su, Xinyan Xiao
arxiv-2502-11514.description: Abstract Recently, inference-time scaling of chain-of-thought (CoT) has been demonstrated as a promising approach for addressing multi-modal reasoning tasks. While existing studies have predominantly centered on text-based thinking, the integration of both visual and textual modalities within the reasoning process remains unexplored. In this study, we pioneer the exploration of inference-time scaling with multi-modal thought, aiming to bridge this gap.

arxiv-2508-03436.title: AI on the Pulse: Real-Time Health Anomaly Detection with Wearable and Ambient Intelligence DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: ; November 10–14, 2025; Coex, Seoul, Korea CCS: Applied computing Life and medical sciences Health informatics CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning Learning paradigms
arxiv-2508-03436.creator: Davide Gabrielli, Bardh Prenkaj, Paola Velardi, Stefano Faralli
arxiv-2508-03436.description: Abstract . We introduce AI on the Pulse, a real-world-ready anomaly detection system that continuously monitors patients using a fusion of wearable sensors, ambient intelligence, and advanced AI models. Powered by UniTS, a state-of-the-art (SoTA) universal time-series model, our framework autonomously learns each patient’s unique physiological and behavioral patterns, detecting subtle deviations that signal potential health risks.

arxiv-2509-08555.title: Benchmarking Optimization Algorithms for Automated Calibration of Quantum Devices
arxiv-2509-08555.creator: Kevin Pack, Shai Machnes, Frank K. Wilhelm
arxiv-2509-08555.description: Abstract We present the results of a comprehensive study of optimization algorithms for the calibration of quantum devices. As part of our ongoing efforts to automate bring-up, tune-up, and system identification procedures, we investigate a broad range of optimizers within a simulated environment designed to closely mimic the challenges of real-world experimental conditions.

arxiv-2509-14121.title: Safe Sliding Mode Control in Position for Double Integrator Systems
arxiv-2509-14121.creator: 1 st Marco A. Gomez, 2 nd Christopher D. Cruz-Ancona
arxiv-2509-14121.description: Abstract We address the problem of robust safety control design for double integrator systems. We show that, when the constraints are defined only on position states, it is possible to construct a safe sliding domain from the dynamic of a simple integrator that is already safe. On this domain, the closed-loop trajectories remain robust and safe against uncertainties and disturbances.

arxiv-2510-19788.title: Benchmarking World-Model Learning
arxiv-2510-19788.creator: Archana Warrier, Thanh Dat Nguyen, Michelangelo Naim, Moksh Jain, Yichao Liang, Karen Schroeder, Cambridge Yang, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Sebastian Vollmer, Kevin Ellis, Zenna Tavares
arxiv-2510-19788.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Archana Warrier, Thanh Dat Nguyen, Michelangelo Naim, Moksh Jain, Yichao Liang, Karen Schroeder, Cambridge Yang, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Sebastian Vollmer, Kevin Ellis, Zenna Tavares. Model-learning agents should gather information to learn world models that support many downstream tasks and inferences, such as predicting unobserved states, estimating near- and far-term consequences of actions, planning action sequences, and detecting changes in dynamics.

CircRNAs are abundantly expressed in eukaryotic organisms and exhibit both location- and step-specificity. In recent years, circRNAs are attracting considerable research attention...

pmc-10670990.title: STXBP6 Gene Mutation: A New Form of SNAREopathy Leads to Developmental Epileptic Encephalopathy
pmc-10670990.creator: Mirella Vinci, Carola Costanza, Rosanna Galati Rando, Simone Treccarichi, Salvatore Saccone, Marco Carotenuto, Michele Roccella, Francesco Calì, Maurizio Elia, Luigi Vetri, Merlin G Butler
pmc-10670990.description: Syntaxin-binding protein 6 (STXBP6), also known as amysin, is an essential component of the SNAP receptor (SNARE) complex and plays a crucial role in neuronal vesicle trafficking. Mutations in genes encoding SNARE proteins are often associated with a broad spectrum of neurological conditions defined as “SNAREopathies”, including epilepsy, intellectual disability, and neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorders.

pmc-12467235.title: Role of the Th2-like Immune Response in Obesity: IL-4 as a Metabolic Regulator and IL-13 as an Effector of Muscle Energy Metabolism
pmc-12467235.creator: Lucía A Méndez-García, Helena Solleiro-Villavicencio, Nallely Bueno-Hernández, Arturo Cérbulo-Vázquez, Galileo Escobedo, Marcela Esquivel-Velázquez, Miguel A Fonseca-Sánchez, Monika Zajkowska
pmc-12467235.description: The Th2 immune response, associated with allergic diseases and helminth infections, has emerged as a significant modulator of metabolic processes in adipose and liver tissues. Th2 cytokines, such as IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13, regulate energy metabolism, insulin resistance, and obesity-related issues. IL-4 and IL-13 play significant roles, while IL-5 mainly recruits eosinophils in visceral fat.

pmc-12590858.title: Impact of integrated clinical case exposure on phase I MBBS students in their learning process in biochemistry
pmc-12590858.creator: Sushma BJ, Gaurav Mishra, RR Sukul, Sumit Parashar
pmc-12590858.description: BackgroundThe integrated clinical case approach connects foundational medical concepts to real-life clinical scenarios, encouraging active problem-solving and interdisciplinary thinking. In contrast, traditional lecture-based teaching often presents subjects in isolation, without emphasizing clinical relevance. This study explores the potential impact of Early Clinical Exposure (ECE) through integrated clinical cases on biochemistry learning among Phase I MBBS students.

pmc-12715378.title: Comparing the posterolateral and the direct lateral approach for cemented hemiarthroplasty after femoral neck fracture: a cost-effectiveness analysis
pmc-12715378.creator: Jonas L ESSER, Maria C J M TOL, Nienke W WILLIGENBURG, Ariena J RASKER, Taco GOSENS, Martijn G M SCHOTANUS, Hanna C WILLEMS, Martin J HEETVELD, J Carel GOSLINGS, Johanna M VAN DONGEN, Rudolf W POOLMAN
pmc-12715378.description: Background and purposeThe 2 most common surgical approaches in hemiarthroplasty for hip fracture treatment are the posterolateral and the direct lateral approach. We aimed to estimate the relative cost-effectiveness of these approaches.MethodsWe conducted an economic evaluation alongside a randomized controlled superiority trial for 6 months.

pmc-12729337.title: Determination of Carotenoids and Their Antioxidant Activity in Fruits of Selected Species from the Genus Rubus and Their Cultivars and Hybrids from Poland Versus Other Regions of the World
pmc-12729337.creator: Natalia Adamczuk, Mirosława Krauze-Baranowska, Marta Milewska, Katarzyna Kimel, Piotr Migas, Wen Qin
pmc-12729337.description: The subject of the study were carotenoids, especially xantophylls in the fruits of various species/cultivars of raspberries, including those cultivated in Poland and those originating from other regions of the world (China, Finland): Rubus occidentalis (5 cultivars); Rubus idaeus (2 cultivars red fruited and 3 cultivars yellow fruited); Rubus chamaemorus; and Rubus chingii and hybrids: R. occidentalis/R.

pmc-12953262.title: Circular Economy Transition in an Emerging Economy: Current Status and Priorities in Peru
pmc-12953262.creator: Alejandro Gallego-Schmid, Ricardo Rebolledo-Leiva, Leonardo Vásquez-Ibarra, Alvaro Elorrieta-Mendoza, Denisse Milagros Paredes Cotohuanca, Claudia E. Henninger, Ana Belén Guerrero
pmc-12953262.description: The circular economy is increasingly recognised as a multidimensional paradigm that goes beyond reducing waste and recycling, encompassing systemic design, regenerative practices, socio-technical innovation, and equity considerations. This study examines Peru’s efforts to transition towards circularity as a representative emerging economy in Latin America, based on 15 semi-structured interviews with stakeholders from academia, policymaking, business, and non-governmental organisations.

pmc-13174246.title: GS-Impute: A neural network framework for accurate imputation of low-density markers in across-population genomic selection
pmc-13174246.creator: Xin Wang, Zhenting Jiang, Tongtong Ding, Ying Cao, Kai Zhou, Guangning Yu, Pengcheng Li, Zefeng Yang, Xuecai Zhang, Shizhong Xu, Yang Xu, Chenwu Xu
pmc-13174246.description: Genomic selection (GS) holds great promise for accelerating breeding progress in plants, and the advancement of across-population GS is essential to realize its full potential. However, conventional across-population GS heavily relies on precisely aligned markers across dense genotypes, whereas the feasibility of using flexible low-density markers remains underexplored.

pmc-13330309.title: Design and practice of the “BOPPPS + PAD” blended learning model in teaching of surgical nursing
pmc-13330309.creator: Meichun Tan, Huyan Zhou, Xiumei Wei, Yunxia Ding, Caiyu Shen, Yutong Wu
pmc-13330309.description: BackgroundSurgical Nursing is a compulsory course for nursing major and plays a crucial role in cultivating nursing professionals. Currently, with the rapid development of educational technology, blended learning that deeply integrates information technology in surgical nursing teaching has become the normality.

pmc-13575379.title: Subclavian central venous catheterization in critically ill children in Türkiye: a safe and feasible approach in a single-center experience
pmc-13575379.creator: Abdulrahman Özel, Esma Nur Özen, Servet Yüce, Sude Menekşe, Hazal Erdem, Merve Boyraz
pmc-13575379.description: BackgroundCentral venous catheter (CVC) insertion is essential procedure in the management of critically ill pediatric patients. However, the optimal catheter insertion site remains controversial due to varying complication rates. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of subclavian vein (SCV) catheterization compared to femoral vein (FV) and internal jugular vein (IJV) access in a pediatric intensive care setting.

pmc-13629814.title: The complete chloroplast genome sequence of Albuca bracteata (Asparagaceae)
pmc-13629814.creator: Youqing Cheng, Tianzi Wang, Yan Zhang, Jinglei Huang, Wenling Shi, Lihan Song, Guoqing Wan
pmc-13629814.description: Albuca bracteata (syn. Ornithogalum caudatum) is an ornamental bulbous plant wth limited plastome data. We assembled its complete chloroplast genome (GenBank PZ425793) from high-throughput sequencing reads. The156.695-bp plastome comprised an 84,786-bp large single-copy region, an 18,555-bp small single-copy region, andtwo 26,677-bp inverted repeats, with 37.66% GC content and 533.8x mean coverage.

pmc-13655255.title: Gonadotropin‐Inhibitory Hormone (GnIH) and Its Receptor GPR147 Mediates Acute Stress‐Induced Activation of the Locus Coeruleus‐SAM Axis
pmc-13655255.creator: Jiani Zhang, Hongyu Zhu, Wenqi Wang, Bingqian Shen, Yuanyuan Xin, Xingxing Song, Xuanyi Lu, Lixuan Li, Siting Chen, Xiaochen Zhang, Jialing Zeng, Haodong Zheng, Jianlong Lao, Ke Peng, Yixian Wei, Jiaming Zheng, Chuanhuo Hu, Xiaoye Wang, Xun Li
pmc-13655255.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Gonadotropin‐inhibitory hormone (GnIH, also known as RFamide‐related peptide‐3, RFRP‐3) is a hypothalamic neuropeptide that regulates vertebrate reproduction via its receptor GPR147. Although GnIH is known to mediate stress‐induced reproductive suppression, its role in broader stress responses remains unclear. This study investigated the fuction of GnIH in acute stress and evaluated the mechanisms by which GnIH regulates norepinephrine (NE) release and activates the locus coeruleus‐sympathetic‐adrenal medulla (LC‐SAM) axis in mice.

zoist-vol-09-1851.title: The Zoist: A Journal of Cerebral Physiology & Mesmerism, Vol. IX (March 1851 to January 1852)
zoist-vol-09-1851.creator: John Elliotson (editor)
zoist-vol-09-1851.description: Vol. IX of The Zoist (1843–1856), the first and most important English journal devoted to mesmerism and cerebral physiology, founded by John Elliotson. Thirteen volumes form the movement's complete primary record: surgical cases, somnambulist reports, and the mesmerism-to-hypnotism debate.
